title: JAPE: Joint Anomaly Prediction and Intrinsic Explanation in Multivariate Time Series
abstract: arXiv:2608.11801v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multivariate time-series anomaly prediction aims to identify whether and when anomalies will occur over a future horizon from historical observations. Existing methods primarily characterize anomalies as deviations in future numerical values, which may overlook subtle dependency changes induced by weak anomaly precursors and provide no native variable-level explanation together with the alert. To bridge these gaps, we propose JAPE, a Joint Anomaly Prediction and Explanation framework that lifts anomaly prediction from numerical-deviation modeling to dependency-structure modeling. JAPE is the first anomaly prediction framework to explicitly model evolving dependency structures for both point-wise alerting and native variable-level explanation. translated_title: JAPE：多元时间序列中的联合异常预测与内在解释
translated_abstract: 多元时间序列异常预测旨在从历史观测中识别未来时间范围内是否以及何时会发生异常。现有方法主要将异常表征为未来数值上的偏差，这可能忽略了由微弱异常前兆引发的细微依赖变化，并且在发出警报时无法提供原生变量级别的解释。为弥补这些差距，我们提出了JAPE，一个联合异常预测与解释框架，将异常预测从数值偏差建模提升至依赖结构建模。JAPE是首个显式建模演化依赖结构的异常预测框架，用于逐点警报和原生变量级解释。具体来说，JAPE (i) 提出了一种解耦时空表示（DSTR）骨干网络，通过可学习的滞后聚合器解耦时间与空间建模，并捕获滞后感知的依赖关系。
tldr: JAPE通过解耦时空表示和依赖结构建模，首次在多元时间序列异常预测中实现原生变量级解释，弥补了传统数值偏差方法的不足。
en_tdlr: JAPE is the first framework to jointly predict anomalies and provide native variable-level explanations in multivariate time series by modeling evolving dependency structures via a decoupled spatio-temporal representation.
